floor.title: The floor
floor.text: After graduation the pool's SOL belongs to the holders. Burn your tokens and the program pays your exact share, in the same transaction. Nobody else's floor moves, the price does not move.

brake.title: The brake
brake.text: No sale, or group of sales, can push the price more than 20 % under the window's high in a minute. What does not fit waits in a queue and is served pro rata, at one price, window after window. Redeeming is never braked.

math.title: What a redeem does to the pool

lede.c: When you redeem x tokens you take exactly S·x/C out of the pool, and the pool burns T·x/C of its own tokens. Both sides shrink in the same proportion, so the floor of the others and the pool price stay where they were. The 0.5 % that stays behind lifts them a little.

math.more: A market sell above the floor does lower it for the others, because the seller takes more than their floor share. That is the only way down, and the brake slows it to 20 % a minute. If the price ever trades under the floor, buying and redeeming is free money, so bots lift it back.
math.note: Default curve numbers: 85 SOL raised, 793.1M tokens sold. Computed with floored-core, the crate the program links.

faq.title: Questions, answered.

what.a: The SOL in a coin's pool divided by the tokens in circulation. It is a balance you can read on chain, not a promise: three accounts and one division. Any holder can take their share at any time with one instruction nobody can block.

zero.q: Can a Cubie coin go to zero?
zero.a: Not while the pool holds SOL and someone holds tokens. The last holder takes the last lamport. The floor can fall when people sell above it, but it can never be withdrawn by anyone.

sell.q: Redeem or sell, which pays more?
sell.a: Above the floor, selling pays more and lowers the floor a little for the others. At or under the floor, redeeming pays more and moves nothing. The coin page shows both numbers side by side before you sign.

brake.q: What happens when the brake engages?
brake.a: The part of your sale that fits under the 20 % limit executes now. The rest goes into a queue, served pro rata of size at the start of every window, same percentage and same price for everyone. You can cancel, claim what you have earned, or switch the rest to the floor instantly.

fees.a: Curve: 1 %, of which 0.3 % is poured into the floor at graduation. Pool: 0.5 %, of which 0.2 % stays in the pool. Redeem: 0.5 %, stays in the pool. Creators get 0.4 % on the curve and 0.2 % after.

verify.q: How do I check it myself?
verify.a: Read pool_sol_vault (minus rent), pool_token_vault, queue_escrow and the mint supply. floor = S / (supply − T − Q). The How it works page does it in your browser for any coin.

faq.lede: Everything on this page can be checked on chain. The full mechanism, with the math, is one click away.

how.title: How the floor works
how.lede: A memecoin whose pool belongs to its holders, with a brake that turns a crash into a staircase. Every number on this page can be checked on chain.

problem.title: The problem
problem.p1: On a classic launchpad, the last holders of a dead coin hold nothing. The liquidity is there, sitting in a pool, but no one can reach it without selling into a price that is already at zero.
problem.p2: Pump burns that liquidity. Its holders paid for it. Cubie gives it back to them.

floor.title: The floor
floor.p1: Once a coin graduates, its pool holds SOL (S) and tokens. Every token outside the pool and outside the brake queue is circulating (C). The floor is S divided by C: what one token can claim from the pool, right now.
floor.p2: Any holder can redeem at any time: burn tokens, receive the exact share of the pool's SOL. A 0.5 % exit fee stays in the pool, so a redemption never lowers the floor for the others. It raises it a hair.
floor.p3: Buys and every fee raise the floor. Market sells above the floor lower it slightly for the others, because they take SOL out at a price above it. Every trade feeds the floor: 0.2 % of each pool trade stays in the pool.

diagram.aria: A pool of SOL, ten circulating token blocks and the floor slab. One block is redeemed: its share of SOL leaves, the slab stays level.
diagram.caption: A holder redeems {x} tokens and receives {sol} SOL. {fee} SOL stays in the pool. The floor does not move down.

brake.title: The brake
brake.p1: A brake window lasts 150 slots, about a minute. Within a window, no sale can push the price more than 20 % below where it started.
brake.alt: A price line stepping down in short stairs, each step held by a yellow brake mark, stopping above the orange floor line
brake.caption: A crash becomes a staircase: at most −20 % per window, above the floor line.
brake.p2: What the window cannot absorb goes into a queue. At the start of each window the queue is sold first, as much as the 20 % limit allows, and the SOL is shared pro rata between everyone queued.
brake.p3: Queued sellers can claim what they have earned, cancel and take their tokens back, or switch to the floor and redeem the rest instantly.

compare.title: Cubie vs Pump
compare.p1: Same curve, same graduation, different ending. What happens to the last 20 % of holders decides everything.
compare.alt: Left: a price line falls through broken ground to zero. Right: the same fall stops in steps on the orange floor line.
compare.left: Pump: the liquidity is burned. The last holders are left with nothing to sell into.
compare.right: Cubie: the liquidity stays under the holders. The last one out still gets their share.
compare.p2: There is no team wallet that can pull the pool. The pool is a program account; only redeem and the swap can move its SOL.

fees.title: Fees

curve.v: 1 %: 0.4 % to the creator, 0.3 % to the protocol, 0.3 % set aside for the floor.

pool.v: 0.5 %: 0.2 % stays in the pool, 0.2 % to the creator, 0.1 % to the protocol.

redeem.v: 0.5 %, kept in the pool for the remaining holders. The last holder pays nothing.

fees.honest: The floor is a current, verifiable minimum, not a promise of future value. If the pool holds little SOL, the floor is low.

zero.q: Can a Cubie coin go to zero?
zero.a: Not after graduation, as long as the pool holds SOL: every circulating token can always be redeemed for its share. Before graduation the coin is on a bonding curve and the floor is only a preview.

promise.q: Is the floor a price guarantee?
promise.a: It is a minimum you can claim today. It moves: buys and fees raise it, market sells above it lower it slightly. It is not a promise about tomorrow's price.

rug.q: What happens if the dev dumps everything?
rug.a: The brake catches it. At most 20 % per window executes, the rest is queued and served pro rata over the next windows. The floor stays where it is. The rug-proof challenge replays exactly that on devnet.

queue.q: My sale was queued. What now?
queue.a: You earn SOL every window as the queue is served. You can claim it, cancel to get your remaining tokens back, or switch to the floor to redeem the rest at once.

creator.a: 0.4 % of curve volume and 0.2 % of pool volume, claimable at any time. The creator cannot touch the pool.

audit.a: The program, the TypeScript SDK and this site are open source. The SDK's math is an exact port of the on-chain core and is tested against it.
